archetypes.name: contract-boundaries
archetypes.rationale: The diff adds new sentinel ordering requirements, a mandatory --scout-manifest-path flag, and a multi-layer scout-manifest pipeline whose invariants span six files; independent contract-boundary review will catch gaps the authors may have normalized.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine every point where a new contract is established: the sentinel ordering requirement in parse-drafter-output.py (summary-before-plan is now enforced, scout-after-plan sentinels are fatal when misplaced), the SCOUT_MANIFEST_PATH flag added to the required-variable loop in both launcher scripts, and the KV output lines emitted on every early-exit path. For each new contract, check whether it is enforced consistently across all callers listed in the docs (launch-codex-drafter.sh, launch-claude-drafter.sh, step2-implement.sh) and whether any caller that was not updated will silently break or get an unhelpful error. Pay particular attention to the backward-compat impact of --scout-manifest-path becoming a hard-required flag rather than optional. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: fail-open-robustness
archetypes.rationale: The diff has a complex fail-open chain (parser writes candidate, launcher filters, moves to canonical path) with multiple temp files and conditional cleanup; any missed cleanup or wrong fail-open/fail-close branch could corrupt state or leave stale scout manifests.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace every code path in scripts/parse-drafter-output.py, scripts/launch-claude-drafter.sh, and scripts/launch-codex-drafter.sh where the scout candidate file might be left behind, overwritten, or silently absent. In particular: (1) the fail() helper deletes scout_tmp before raising SystemExit — does this correctly handle the case where scout_tmp was never created? (2) In the launcher shells, _filter_status is extracted from the filter wrapper's stdout with awk; what happens when the wrapper emits no SCOUT_STATUS= line and _filter_status is empty — does the condition `"$_filter_status" != "parse-failed"` incorrectly pass? (3) Verify that every early-exit path in both launchers (CODEX_EXEC_FAILED, CODEX_EMPTY_OUTPUT, parse failure) removes both _scout_candidate and _scout_filtered. (4) In plan_contains_standalone_scout_manifest(), when the loop ends still inside a fence (in_fence=True), the function falls back to using the full plan_text for regex scanning — confirm this is intentional and correct. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: integration-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The scout sidecar pipeline touches dispatch-panel.sh, review-core.sh, review-and-fix.sh, run-step5-review.sh, and step2-implement.sh — which are not in this round-3 diff — so verifying cross-script integration completeness requires checking whether those callers were updated or whether they will silently pass the wrong arguments.
archetypes.prompt_body: This diff adds --scout-manifest-path as a required flag to launch-codex-implement.sh and launch-cursor-implement.sh, and emits SCOUT_MANIFEST_WRITTEN in their stdout KV envelopes. Read the actual current content of skills/implement/scripts/step2-implement.sh to confirm it passes --scout-manifest-path to both launchers and reads SCOUT_MANIFEST_WRITTEN from their stdout. Similarly read scripts/run-step5-review.sh to confirm it uses step2-external-scout-eligible.txt (not step2-spawn-coder.txt) as the eligibility marker, and reads scout-coder-manifest.json. If those files were not updated in this round, identify the specific missing wiring. Also check whether SCOUT_MANIFEST_WRITTEN=false on early-exit paths (cap_hit, auth-prep failure, model-args failure) is correctly handled by the dispatcher — does a false value on those paths cause incorrect behavior? Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
